title: This Spanish city is older than Rome.

beats.text: This Spanish city is older than Rome.
Nearly three thousand years ago, sailors from Tyre, in today's Lebanon, crossed the whole Mediterranean, and kept going.
On an island off southern Spain they built a trading port. They called it Gadir. We call it Cádiz.
Ancient writers dated it to around 1100 BC. Archaeologists have found remains from at least the 800s BC. Either way: older than Rome.
beats.say: Ancient writers dated it to around eleven hundred B C. Archaeologists have found remains from at least the eight hundreds B C. Either way: older than Rome.

beats.text: They came for silver from the mines of southern Spain, and for tuna. The city even put tuna on its coins.
Its great temple honoured the god Melqart. The Greeks and Romans called him Hercules.
In 1887, workers in Cádiz dug up a marble Phoenician coffin, with a man's face carved on the lid.
beats.say: In eighteen eighty-seven, workers in Cádiz dug up a marble Phoenician coffin, with a man's face carved on the lid.

beats.text: Under Rome, Gadir became Gades. Julius Caesar made all its citizens Romans.
Three thousand years on, people still live there. Many call it the oldest city in Western Europe.
